newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. official says China textile talks progress.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official says China textile talks progress.

text.p: China and the United States are making progress in talks to extend a bilateral textile accord and resolve a dispute over U.S. penalties on Chinese exports, U.S. textile negotiator Rita Hayes said on Wednesday.
"We are gradually reaching agreement on some of the issues, but we still have a lot of different issues to settle," Hayes said after a morning meeting with Chinese trade officials.
Both Washington and Beijing hoped to reach agreement before the Friday deadline for renewal of their 1994 textile trade accord, she said.
The Sino-U.S. textile pact had been scheduled to expire on December 31 but was extended by one month to allow both sides time to hammer out a compromise.

Washington and Beijing were also seeking to ease a dispute over Chinese exports of textiles via third countries that have prompted U.S. threats of multi-million dollar penalties and raised the spectre of a cross-Pacific trade war.
"Both sides are in hopes that we can reach agreement by the end of the week," said Hayes, who began a scheduled three days of talks in the Chinese capital on Tuesday.

"We have made what I think is slow progress but good progress," she told Reuters. "We will probably go late into the night and hopefully we can solve some of the issues that we didn't solve this morning."
Chinese officials have also voiced optimism about the outcome of the negotiations, saying a resolution would be good for both sides.
"We are maintaining an optimistic attitude towards the prospects of these textile talks," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing on Tuesday.
Washington slapped $19 million worth of penalties on imports of Chinese textiles last September, saying Beijing was shipping textiles through third countries to evade quota restrictions.
China has threatened to retaliate by temporarily banning imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks but has delayed such action to allow time for further talks.

China's large textile exports to U.S. and European customers have long been a source of dispute but have in recent years become especially sensitive for U.S. trade officials eager to reduce Washington's swelling trade deficit.
